Never trust IPO hype. A nine thousand crore IPO just closed, and retail bid for only forty eight percent of its quota. Why?
It's Mahanadi Coalfields, Coal India's miner in Odisha. Two hundred eighteen million tonnes of coal, and over ten thousand crore profit last year.
Price band, one twenty nine to one thirty six rupees. But it's all an offer for sale. Coal India is selling. No new money goes to the company.
But here's the strange part. A smaller IPO closed the same week, and it was subscribed almost eighteen times.
Crystal Crop Protection. Crop sprays and seeds, a four hundred fifty five crore issue. Rich investors bid thirty nine times. Retail, almost ten.
Mahanadi's final count? One point five times. Institutions, five times. Retail, just zero point four eight.
So does big demand mean a big listing? Look at E triple A India Alternatives. Five point three times subscribed. It opened just zero point six percent above issue.
It closed day one up three point eight percent, and by November twenty three, up nine point four. Subscription shows demand, not the listing price. Crystal lists Thursday. Mahanadi, Friday.
